cells.tense: You're feeling with this person right now and you still know where your own feet are.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're already carrying for someone. Tell them you're choosing to carry it this week.
cells.core:
You feel with people and you stay yourself while you do it. That sounds ordinary until you watch how often it isn't there — people either go hard and lose contact, or they go soft and vanish into whoever is standing in front of them. You do neither. You can stand beside someone in something difficult and still know where you end.

So the care you give actually lands. It doesn't arrive as rescue and it doesn't arrive as a bill they'll owe later. The person across from you can take it and keep their own footing. What this can hold next is staying power — you can keep holding someone's hard week without going rigid about it. Pick one thing you're carrying and say out loud that you chose it. Saying it is what keeps it yours.
cells.sheetLine: You feel with people without disappearing into them.
cells.verb: feeling with someone without losing the line between you
cells.place: in the choosing of where your attention and effort go

cells.tense: You're bracing for how this will land before the person in front of you has said a word.
cells.ask: Before you answer anyone today, wait one beat and ask whose feeling this is to act on.
cells.core:
You're ahead of people. You take on what they might need before they've said it, and it's already yours to fix by the time the conversation starts. The caring is real. But nothing on either side is being sorted anymore — a mood across the table lands in you as your job, and you answer it before it's even asked.

You'd call that being thoughtful. Part of it is. The part where you decide where your effort goes has gone quiet though, and it's other people's days that are running your week. What ends here isn't the caring. It's the automatic yes that fires off before you've had a second to check whose feeling this actually is.
cells.sheetLine: You take on other people's days before they arrive.
cells.verb: feeling with someone without losing the line between you
cells.place: in the choosing of where your attention and effort go

cells.tense: You stood at a closed door a long time ago and never quite came back through it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true small thing about your day, with no purpose behind it.
cells.core:
You've gone flat, and it's steady. Feeling with people became something you turned down, and turning it down worked well enough that you kept doing it. The relationships you have are real, but they stay shallow, and nobody gets closer than arm's length.

Warmth isn't the thing that's gone. Don't try to manufacture feeling or force yourself open. What's empty is the part of you that decides where to lean — the small directional move, the one that says 'this person, today.' So don't push the feeling. Do one deliberate thing with someone. Tell them one true small thing about your day, unprompted, no agenda in it. That tiny decision is the muscle, and it comes back one call at a time.
cells.sheetLine: The relationships are real but they stay at the surface.
cells.verb: feeling with someone without losing the line between you
cells.place: in the choosing of where your attention and effort go

cells.tense: The care is running right now in how you show up, and you keep calling it being practical.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today because you cared, and say so plainly when someone asks.
cells.core:
People come to you and leave steadier. You know that, and you file it under being useful. What's happening underneath is that you feel with them — it's why you notice, why you show up, why you arrange the thing before anyone has to ask. The caring is doing the work while you tell yourself it's just efficiency.

Here's the part you keep leaving out: you can feel that you feel for these people. When the subject comes up, that much is legible to you. You've been letting it read as indifference because saying it would put something of yours on the table. It's already on the table. Saying it is what would move it back into your hands.
cells.sheetLine: It's care, and it's yours. You've just been filing it as practical.

cells.place: in the choosing of where your attention and effort go

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a reader can reliably feel another's warmth as choice rather than accident while believing none of it is theirs — the record only supports authorship running while the claim on it hasn't been made, not how the other person experiences it. A reader could reasonably say the real issue is schedule or plain fatigue, not the capacity being spent ahead of time. The asks survive being wrong: they are small acts that teach something regardless of the diagnosis. The sentence serving the writer more than them is 'The care is already moving — you've just been calling it logistics.' It is the kind of line that fits the archive well; I am replacing it with a plainer version under the Unacknowledged cell so the person is not flattered into a costume.
